title: Step 1: Hook - The TV Remote War!
text: Imagine it's Sunday evening. You want to watch your favorite cartoon, but your brother wants to watch a cricket match. Your father wants to watch the news, and your mother wants to watch a serial. Everyone wants the TV remote! Who gets to decide?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking - Making Fair Choices
text: Why do you think families have arguments over small things like TV remotes or what to cook for dinner? If you were the head of the family, how would you solve the TV remote war without making anyone sad?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - The Balance of Happiness
content.description: Just like a seesaw needs balance so that both children can play, a family needs a balance of decisions where everyone gets a turn.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Family Conflicts and Compromise
text: Differences in choices are called 'Conflicts'. When people in a family want different things, it can lead to quarrels. However, loving families solve these by making a 'Compromise' - an agreement where everyone gets a little bit of what they want. It is important to listen to everyone's opinion.

content.preview: An agreement where both sides give up a little to reach a solution.
A disagreement or argument between people.

content.question: What is the best way to solve a disagreement in a family?
options: Shouting and crying until you get your way.
Listening to everyone and finding a compromise.
Ignoring everyone and leaving the room.
Letting only the oldest person decide everything.

content.title: Don't Forget!
content.text: Many people think that 'fighting' and 'conflicts' are the same. A conflict is just having different opinions. It only becomes a bad fight when we stop listening to each other!

title: Step 6: Reflection - Your Experience
text: Think about the last time you had a quarrel with your sibling or friend. How did it end? Did you find a compromise, or did an elder have to step in and make a rule?

title: Step 7: Connection - Democracy at Home
text: Did you know that taking everyone's opinion before making a decision is called 'Democracy'? Just like citizens vote for their leaders in a country, taking a family vote for Sunday dinner is practicing democracy at home!

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - The Family Rulebook
content.text: Create a 'Family Rulebook' with your parents and siblings. Write down 3 rules on how decisions will be made when there is a disagreement (like who gets the TV remote or what game to play).

title: Step 1: Hook - The Different Rules
text: Pratibha is hurrying home because it's 7 PM. Her brothers, Sandeep and Sanjay, are still playing outside. Nobody tells them to rush home. But if Pratibha is late, her parents get very worried and angry. Have you noticed different rules for different people in the same house?

title: Step 2: Socratic Thinking - Is it Fair?
text: Why do you think there are different rules for boys and girls in some families? Do you think it is fair that boys can play late but girls must come home early? What would happen if rules were the same for everyone?

content.title: Step 3: Discovery - The Scale of Equality
content.description: Imagine a weighing scale. If you put different weights on both sides, the scale tips over and becomes unfair. Similarly, having different rules for boys and girls makes the 'Scale of Equality' unbalanced.

title: Step 4: Reveal - Gender Equality
text: The idea that boys and girls should have the same rights, rules, and opportunities is called 'Gender Equality'. In many traditional homes, girls face stricter rules because of old fears and customs. But today, the world is changing, and it's important to have equal rules for both boys and girls!

content.preview: Treating everyone fairly and in the same way, regardless of who they are.

content.title: A note for parents and teachers
content.text: Encourage students to question traditions respectfully. Discussing gender roles helps children build critical thinking skills.

content.question: If your sister wants to play cricket but some relatives say 'girls don't play cricket', what should you do?
options: Tell her to stop playing and go inside.
Support her and invite her to play with your team.
Tell her to play a different game.

title: Step 6: Reflection - Rule Changing
text: If you could change one rule in your house that you feel is unfair, what would it be? Explain your reason to yourself or write it in your journal.

title: Step 7: Connection - Laws of the Country
text: Just like a home should have equal rules, our country, India, has a Constitution that promises 'Right to Equality'. It says the law is the same for every citizen, whether they are a man or a woman!

content.title: Step 8: Mastery - Equal Timetable
content.text: Make a daily timetable for a brother and sister. Distribute the household chores (like setting the table, folding clothes) equally between them so that nobody does more work than the other!
